name: Mercado de Todos
summary: Mercado de Todos is a popular swap meet-style market in La Mesa, Tijuana, featuring numerous vendor stalls selling phone accessories, electronics, video games, clothing, bags, and shoes. With nearly 6,000 reviews and a 4.2-star rating, this bustling marketplace offers budget-friendly shopping in an authentic mercado atmosphere.
demographics: Mercado de Todos primarily serves working-class and middle-income Hispanic families in the La Mesa neighborhood of Tijuana, with a strong cross-border shopping component from San Diego County residents seeking affordable goods. The typical visitor demographic skews toward budget-conscious shoppers aged 25-55, including young families and bargain hunters looking for electronics, clothing, and accessories at competitive prices. The trade area encompasses the eastern Tijuana metropolitan area, drawing customers who appreciate the swap meet atmosphere and value-oriented merchandise mix that caters to both local residents and international visitors.
description: Mercado de Todos, located on Boulevard Gustavo Díaz Ordaz in La Mesa, Tijuana, is a vibrant swap meet-style shopping destination that has become a cornerstone of the local retail landscape. This unfussy market brings together dozens of vendor stalls offering an eclectic mix of merchandise, from phone accessories and video games to movies, clothing, bags, and shoes, creating a bustling marketplace atmosphere that appeals to bargain hunters and everyday shoppers alike. Operating daily from 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, the center has earned a solid 4.2-star rating from nearly 6,000 reviews, testament to its popularity among both local residents and cross-border shoppers. The market's informal layout and diverse vendor offerings create an authentic shopping experience that stands in contrast to traditional enclosed malls, with each stall providing personalized service and competitive pricing. As a community gathering place in the La Mesa district, Mercado de Todos serves as more than just a shopping center—it's a cultural hub where families can find affordable goods while enjoying the social atmosphere of a traditional Mexican mercado.
